As his channel grew, Donaldson hired four childhood friends – Kris Tyson (formerly Chris Tyson), Chandler Hallow, Garrett Ronalds and Jake Franklin – to contribute to his channel.[34] They then contacted numerous YouTubers in order to obtain statistics of their successful videos and predict the platform's recommendation system.[40][*clarification needed*] Franklin left the crew in 2020. In fall 2016, Donaldson dropped out of East Carolina University to pursue a full-time career as a YouTuber.[17][37] His mother did not approve of this and made him move out of the family home.[34]


As his channel grew, Donaldson hired four childhood friends – Kris Tyson (formerly Chris Tyson), Chandler Hallow, Garrett Ronalds and Jake Franklin – to contribute to his channel.[34] They then contacted numerous YouTubers in order to obtain statistics of their successful videos and predict the platform's recommendation system.[40][*clarification needed*] Franklin left the crew in 2020. Based on my search of Wikipedia articles, I can provide the start years for the top four most subscribed YouTube channels:

1. **T-Series** - 2006 (joined YouTube on March 13, 2006)
2. **MrBeast** - 2012 (Jimmy Donaldson began posting videos in 2012, with his early "Worst intros on YouTube" series)
3. **Cocomelon** - 2006 (the channel started posting videos in September 2006 under the name "ABC Kid TV")
4. **PewDiePie** - 2010 (Felix Kjellberg created his current channel in 2010, though he had an earlier account that he abandoned)

**Summary:**
- T-Series: 2006
- MrBeast: 2012 
- Cocomelon: 2006
- PewDiePie: 2010

Note that these start years represent when these channels began posting content to YouTube, which may differ from when they were first created or when their current channel names were adopted. The information is based on what was available in the Wikipedia articles I accessed.
